## Goal

**As an** operator, **I want** a measured verdict on the two chain/routing fixes shipped on 2026-11-03, **so that** "it is fixed" is a claim backed by a like-for-like before/after comparison against the configuration's own scheduled windows — not by the absence of complaints.

**Earliest implementation time: 2026-11-04 04:00 UTC.** That is the end of the first remote-closed window (`01:00-04:00` UTC) that completes after the 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC restart, so it is the first instant with (a) ≥13.5 h of post-fix log and (b) a full scheduled-gap sample. See **Timing** for why 2026-11-04 10:00 UTC is the *preferred* like-for-like point.

discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK, discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5.

## What is deployed

| Item | Commit | What it should change |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK — fail fast on a provably dead chain | `7892d22d` | no chain hold when every provider is deterministically skipped or terminally refused; earliest-reset `Retry-After`; a `remote-ok` request is never bounced onto a chain with no capacity |
| LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 — diagnosable lease occupancy | `763ed61f` | `local_dispatch_denied` carries the full occupancy evidence; `local_occupancy_divergence` names contradictions; stale records cannot block |

Deployed by restart **2026-11-03 14:25:09–14:25:10 UTC** (proxy pid 158427; `llama-server` and TTS relaunched and all three healthy). **The post-fix measurement window starts at 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC** (log rotation line `14:25:10,847 - INFO - Rotated previous proxy log`). Anything before that line is pre-fix.

## Timing: when the fix can actually fire

`model=code` has 7 providers; the gates that create a *provably dead* chain are the `available_times` windows:

| Provider | `available_times` (UTC) | Closed |
|---|---|---|
| `local-qwen3` | unrestricted | — |
| `munitoai-free` | unrestricted | gated only by usage-limit reset / quota |
| `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `deepseek-flash` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `munitoai` | `10:00-23:00` | **23:00–10:00** |

So the chain is *window*-dead only in **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00** UTC, and it is only *provably* dead when `munitoai-free` is also out (usage-limit reset / quota) — which is exactly the 2026-11-03 08:41 shape. `munitoai-free`'s recorded reset was `2026-11-04T00:02Z`, so **the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 may legitimately have a live provider and therefore no trigger**; that is correct behaviour, not evidence of anything.

Therefore:

- **earliest defensible evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **04:00 UTC** (first complete post-fix gap);
- **preferred like-for-like evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **10:00 UTC**, i.e. the end of the `06:00–10:00` gap — the same clock window as the baseline below;
- if neither gap produced a trigger, conclude **inconclusive** (say so explicitly) and re-check at the next gap or at the next usage-limit/quota block rather than recording a fake pass.

## Baseline (pre-fix)

Recorded evidence, for the record:

- 2026-11-03 **08:41:42** — every remote provider deterministically skipped (`munitoai-free` `usage_limit_reset_pending` reset ~15.4 h away; `opencode-go-3` `quota_exhausted` ~14 days; four entries `outside_available_window`) and the proxy logged `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s before restarting cycle` **three times**. The audit subprocess (`audit-RISE-0MVZEOVQG0075XSU-...`) received a 429 in 0.4 s and could never succeed; its 1080 s per-call screen budget was consumed by holds.
- 2026-11-03 **08:40:05** — `Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted message ... (status=400)` followed immediately by two 300 s holds (the first provider's raw 400 carried no `Retry-After`, which is what re-enabled the "legacy full hold").
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:40** — local guard refused with `eta_prefill_s=45.2 enforced=true` and the request was routed onto the dead remote chain (`outcome=exhausted`); **08:50:41** the identical prompt and identical ETA were admitted (`enforced=false`, `eta_occupancy_s=0.0`) and produced a first byte in 6 s.
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:31.690** — `local_dispatch_denied session=... owner=... active=1` on a two-slot pool while `/llama/local/status` at 08:49:31.034 reported `available_slots=2`: the refusal named an owner and a count but not which gate refused.

### Measured baseline — log file `proxy.log.2026-11-03_101625`, window 08:37:26 → 10:16:25 UTC (99 min)

This is the pre-fix window captured by the log rotated at the 10:16 restart. It sits inside the `06:00–10:00` closed gap, i.e. it is the like-for-like comparison window.

| Signal | Count (99 min) |
|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted for model=` (holds taken) | **105** — 36 of them `holding 300s`, plus 30 s / 120 s / 38 s / 17 s variants |
| `All providers exhausted for model=` | 189 |
| deterministic-skip vocabulary | `usage_limit_reset_pending` 1198 · `outside its available_times window` 884 · `quota_exhausted` 1230 |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` | 137 |
| … of which `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` | **57** (11 distinct sessions) |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 26 (none carrying occupancy evidence) |

### Control window — open windows, no trigger expected

`proxy.log`, 10:16:29 → 13:34:50 UTC (3 h 18 m; remote windows **open** that whole time): `Chain exhausted` **0**, `All providers exhausted` **0**, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` 334 (46 × `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — correct fall-throughs, because remote had capacity), `local_dispatch_denied` 97. Use this as the "no trigger + open chain" reference: it shows what a *healthy* zero looks like, and it is why "0 holds" alone proves nothing.

Log retention is 7 days (`Pruned old rotated log ... > 7 days old`), so the baseline file survives until ~2026-11-10. Re-extract the numbers above if it is needed after that; do not assume it is still there.

## Measurement technique

Rules that keep the comparison honest:

1. **Like-for-like windows only.** Compare post-fix samples taken inside a *closed* window (`01:00–04:00` / `06:00–10:00` UTC) against the baseline above. Never compare an open-window sample against it; an open chain cannot trigger the fix, so it will always look "fixed".
2. **Normalise per hour** — sample lengths will differ; report counts per hour as well as raw counts.
3. **Check chain aliveness before interpreting a zero.** If no trigger fired, prove the chain was actually provably dead in that window (`munitoai-free` unavailable *and* the four window-gated providers closed). A zero with a live chain is `inconclusive`, not `fixed`.
4. **Exclude the restart verification probe** from the sample: session `verify-lp-0mw0kzr7a003ufqk-restart` (2026-11-03 14:25:54, 18/8/26 tokens) exists only to prove the deploy.
5. **Quote the log line, not the count**, for anything that decides the verdict — a count can be satisfied by a wrong reason.

### LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (fail fast / no bounce) — expected post-fix signatures

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log            # or the rotated file covering the chosen window
# 1. the fail-fast line replaces the hold, on one vocabulary
grep -c 'chain_planned_unavailable'          $LOG    # expect > 0 in a provably-dead window
grep -m3 'chain_planned_unavailable'         $LOG    # inspect reason=, hold=skipped, retry_after=, deterministic_skips=, terminal=
# 2. no hold on a provably dead chain
grep -c 'Chain exhausted for model='         $LOG    # expect 0 in that window (baseline: 105/99 min)
# 3. the local override instead of a bounce onto a dead chain
grep -c 'local_admission_guard_local_wait'   $LOG    # expect > 0 where the old code emitted direct_fallback
grep 'local_admission_guard_direct_fallback' $LOG | grep -c 'reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct'   # expect 0 *while the chain is dead* (baseline 57)
# 4. retry timing is honest (earliest reset, body == header, capped)
grep 'chain_planned_unavailable' $LOG | grep -o 'retry_after=[0-9]*' | sort -u
# 5. the client-visible shape (the preserved first error, now timed)
grep 'Returning first provider error response' $LOG | tail -3
# 6. the report renders the new section
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24   # "## Chain-end outcomes"
```

Targets:

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted` (holds) per closed-window hour | 105 / 1.65 h ≈ **64/h** | **0** where every skip is deterministic; unchanged for transient chains (cooldown / 5xx / connection error) — verify at least one transient hold still occurs |
| `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped` | 0 (line did not exist) | > 0, one per affected request (not per provider) |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` with a dead chain | 57 / 99 min | **0**, replaced by `local_admission_guard_local_wait` |
| `All providers exhausted` reached from a local ETA refusal | the 08:49:40 shape | **0** |
| audit-* call latency on a doomed chain | 300 s × 3 holds before the error | < 1 s |
| Advertised `retry_after` | cap-derived (3600) or absent | the earliest known reset, capped by `max_retry_after_seconds`, equal to the `Retry-After` header |

Per-line acceptance (AC2/AC4 of the item):
- `local_admission_guard_local_wait` must appear **with** `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` and **without** a following `→ routing to next provider` line;
- `chain_planned_unavailable` must **not** appear in a window where a provider was merely cooling down (that would be a false positive — the verdict must stay conservative).

### LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 (diagnostics) — this half is measurable within hours

Denials happen under local contention (26 in 99 min pre-fix; 97 in 3 h 18 m), so this verdict does not need a closed window:

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
# every denial must carry the evidence suffix (fields: records_total, records_active,
# records_unexpired, records_stale, active_counter, max_local, generating,
# prefill_in_flight, prefill_cap, llama_available_slots, llama_total_slots, records=…)
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied'                                  $LOG
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied.*records_total='                  $LOG    # expect == the count above
# contradictions are logged, and the "our own numbers cannot explain it" class must be zero
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=llama_reports_free_slots'  $LOG   # > 0 is fine (prefill cap vs llama view)
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=occupancy_unexplained'     $LOG   # must be 0 — non-zero is a bookkeeping defect, file it
# which cap refused is now readable without a repro
grep -m3 'local_dispatch_denied' $LOG | grep -o 'generating=[0-9]*\|prefill_in_flight=[0-9]*\|prefill_cap=[0-9]*\|max_local=[0-9]*'
```

Targets: 100 % of `local_dispatch_denied` lines carry the evidence; `occupancy_unexplained` **0**; the 08:49:31 question ("denied with `available_slots=2` — which gate?") answerable from the line alone (expect `prefill_in_flight=1 prefill_cap=1`, i.e. the serialised-prefill cap, for that shape).

## Decision criteria

| Outcome | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **fixed** | a provably-dead window shows ≥1 `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped`, **0** holds, and the evidence suffix on every denial | close with the numbers; no follow-up |
| **partial** | fail-fast fires but a hold still occurs on a deterministic chain, or a denial lacks the evidence suffix | file a `test-failure`/bug item naming the exact line and reason; do not close |
| **not fixed** | a provably-dead window still shows `Chain exhausted` / `direct_fallback`, and no `chain_planned_unavailable` | reopen LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (or file a new bug) with the window and the log lines |
| **inconclusive** | no provably-dead window occurred in the sample | record it, keep the item open, re-check at the next gap/usage-limit block; never record a pass |
| **regression** | holds disappear on *transient* chains too (cooldown/5xx), or `occupancy_unexplained` > 0 | treat as a defect: the verdict is over-firing |

If any outcome requires code change, create the follow-up item (`discovered-from:<this id>`) and implement it in its own worktree — this item is measurement only.

## Out of scope

- Changing provider `available_times` or adding an always-on remote provider (the operator rejected that on 2026-10-31; see LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN).
- Extending the classifier or the `chain_planned_unavailable` vocabulary — that is now owned by epic LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN (its AC11, extend-never-fork).
- Re-litigating the incident's per-call budget arithmetic.

## Candidate follow-up observed during the restart (not measured here)

Before the 2026-11-03 14:25 restart, `/llama/local/status` reported `llama_server_running=true`, `available_slots=2/2`, `capacity_hint=idle` for ~3 hours while **no `llama-server` process existed** (`llama-server.log` ends `start-llama.sh: line 273: 4168 Killed` at 11:33) and local dispatches were failing with `ConnectError`. `/health` said `healthy` throughout. That is a stale *running-state* divergence (distinct from the slot-count divergence fixed in LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5): file it separately with this evidence if it reproduces — it is a candidate for the same "engine view vs route view" family.

## Assumptions

- The deployed code is what runs: proxy started 14:25:09 UTC, `dev` HEAD `7892d22d` committed 12:54 — confirm again at evaluation time with `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` and `git log -1 --format=%cI dev`.
- `munitoai-free` remains the only unrestricted remote, so every provably-dead window is of the shape above; if a provider is added or re-timed, re-derive the window table before comparing.
- The 7-day log retention is long enough to reach the earliest evaluation date; if it is not, the baseline numbers in this description are the record.

## Scheduling hold (do NOT implement before the gate instant)

The title carries the earliest instant, but a title cannot stop `wl next` from
dispatching this item tonight, which would produce a premature sample. The item
is therefore parked with a **descriptive timer hold** as its assignee:
`not-before-2026-11-04T04:00Z` (a non-empty assignee is a scheduling hold, so
`wl next` skips it). This is a timer label, not an agent claim — no agent owns
this item.

At or after **2026-11-04 04:00 UTC**, release it and implement:

```bash
wl update LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --assignee "" --json    # release the timer hold
wl show LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --json                    # then /skill:implement <id>
```

If you are reading this *before* the gate instant because someone released the
hold early, do not measure: say so, re-apply the hold, and wait for the first
complete closed window. If the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 turns out to have a

## Summary

Reproduce the intake's fossil case in a test: a stale `/slots` detail snapshot keeps reporting `is_processing=true` / `phase=decode` for a dispatch the proxy already released (`prefill_deadline` / `lease_evicted`), while `local_abandoned_slots=0`.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_progress_staleness.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/llama/local/status` does not report a slot as `generating`/`decode` for a dispatch the proxy has already released: the slot is annotated with the existing `abandoned` vocabulary (`abandoned`, `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_scope`), or the stale citation is dropped from the payload.
- On the released-dispatch scenario, `local_abandoned_slots` accounts for the slot and no slot carries `phase=decode` for that session.
- Both registry shapes are covered: the exact `(endpoint, slot)` entry and the endpoint-wide entry — including the shape where a stale owner binding keeps `owner_session_id` non-null.
- The TTL boundary is covered: an entry younger than `DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS` annotates, and an expired entry must not resurrect a fossil (the slot is dropped, never relabelled live).
- The fresh (non-stale) path is asserted unchanged: a live proxy-owned decode slot is never annotated abandoned and never dropped.
- The tests fail against the current code, recording the defect that LP-0MW3ED60P009GXR9 fixes.

## Root-cause candidates (recorded here, settled in LP-0MW3ED60P009GXR9)

1. `_record_abandoned_slot` is never called on the `lease_evicted` / `prefill_deadline` release paths.
2. TTL expiry (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS = 900.0`) is shorter than the observed snapshot age — the fossil read was ~360 s after release, so a miss here would be surprising but must be ruled out.
3. `_clear_abandoned_slot` cleared by another path's *fresh* `/slots` read (SSE broadcast / enrichment path) between release and the status poll.
4. The endpoint-wide annotation guard (`is_processing and owner_session_id is None`) blocked because the slot-owner map still bound the released slot to the old session — that produces exactly the observed shape (`phase=decode` owned by a released session, `local_abandoned_slots=0`).

The abandonment machinery already exists (LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB, LP-0MVUVHB1V006HA5I); this is a defect in that path, not missing machinery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The root cause is recorded on this item: which of the four candidates listed in the LP-0MW3ED4GL00886TO child (missing `_record_abandoned_slot`, TTL expiry, premature `_clear_abandoned_slot`, endpoint-wide guard blocked by a stale owner binding) produced the 2026-11-03 fossil, evidenced by the LP-0MW3ED4GL00886TO reproduction.

## Goal

A test that keeps the documented per-prompt cache geometry and the configured `cache-ram` in sync, so the number can never drift from its derivation again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test parses `models.ini`, reads `cache-ram` and `ctx-checkpoints`, and asserts the configured value matches the documented derivation (32 checkpoints × ~62.8 MiB ≈ 2.0 GiB per prompt, times the supported concurrent-prompt count, plus the stated margin) and stays above the stated `MemAvailable` floor headroom rule.
- [ ] The test fails if the comment's documented geometry and the configured value diverge (e.g. a checkpoint-count change without re-deriving `cache-ram`).
- [ ] The test states the host budget it assumes (**128 GiB unified memory**, producer-confirmed) and skips with a clear reason — never silently passes — if the host geometry cannot be derived.
- [ ] The red run is recorded in a work-item comment.

1. Add a fixture that computes the expected `cache-ram` from `ctx-checkpoints` and the per-checkpoint size constant.
2. Assert the configured value equals the computed one (or is within the documented rounding/margin).
3. Reuse `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`'s recommendation rule where practical rather than duplicating the arithmetic.

- `./models.ini` (`cache-ram`, `ctx-checkpoints`)

Implementation slice for AC3 (re-derive `cache-ram` from per-prompt geometry, with a MemAvailable floor).

## Goal

Express and verify the `cache-ram` headroom in **per-prompt checkpoint geometry** terms and pin a MemAvailable floor, so the number is derived from evidence rather than inherited.

**Duplicate check:** `LP-0MV5HSUHF002MDPG` (completed) already raised the cap to **40,960 MiB** from a measured 2,013 MiB/prompt × 16 × 1.25 derivation. That part needs no redo. This slice covers only the remaining gaps: the *checkpoint-geometry* derivation the AC asks for (32 checkpoints × ~62.8 MiB ≈ 2.0 GiB/prompt + weights), an explicit **MemAvailable floor**, and a measurement refresh.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The per-prompt geometry is stated in checkpoint terms from a **fresh** measurement (`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`): checkpoints × per-checkpoint MiB, plus weights, and the resulting supported concurrent-prompt count — recorded in the item comment with the exact command and date.
- [ ] `models.ini` records the derivation **and** the MemAvailable floor at which the documented fallback (reduce slot count / cap concurrent prompts) must trigger; the floor is tied to the existing host-pressure signal (`host_pressure.py` thresholds) rather than a new untracked number.
- [ ] The configured `cache-ram` is either unchanged (derivation shows 40,960 MiB is still correct) or raised only as far as the floor permits — never lowered below the measured requirement.
- [ ] `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` states the same derivation and floor; the cache geometry sync test passes.
- [ ] No slot-count change (LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 territory).

- [ ] Parent AC traceability — **Cache headroom sized from evidence** — `cache-ram` re-derived from per-prompt state geometry (≈2 GiB at 32 checkpoints × 62.8 MiB + weights). Host has **128 GiB unified memory** (producer-confirmed), so raising `cache-ram` is permitted up to a stated MemAvailable floor; the derivation and floor are recorded in models.ini comment style, and a doc/test keeps the documented geometry and the configured value in sync.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Run `prompt_cache_analysis.py --recommend` over the current cache-state corpus and capture the checkpoint term and weight term.
2. Update the `models.ini` comment block (derivation + floor) and the tuning doc.
3. Verify with the changed-scope test run.

- `proxy/proxy/host_pressure.py`
- `./models.ini` (`cache-ram`, `ctx-checkpoints`)
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`

## Finding

The proxy's log retention (7 days: `logging.retention_days` default in
`proxy/proxy/utils.py:1034`, which makes `TimedRotatingFileHandler` keep
`backupCount = 7 × 24 / 6 = 28` six-hour segments, with `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy`
as a `rotate 7` daily safety net) is shorter than the age a committed
measurement record reaches before it is audited or re-examined.

Concrete instance: `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` had to restate the pre-change baseline
on the window `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` (8 days before the
implementing session). The window was measured in full on 2026-10-30, but by
2026-11-05 the first ~16 h of `2026-10-28` had been pruned: only
`proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` (16:16:14→22:16:12) and
`proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015.gz` (00:00:00→00:10:15) survive — **6 h 10 m of a
24 h window (25.7 %, 67 of 136 enqueued waits)**. The committed record
therefore carries two provenance classes (measurement-time full window vs
today's coverage re-measurement) instead of a single regenerable artefact.

This is a recurring shape, not a one-off: any "measure a window, then commit a
record" slice that lands more than ~7 days after its window has to be
documented as un-reproducible, and every AC of the form "re-running the
embedded command regenerates the committed JSON" degrades to "regenerable
while the archives survive".

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a measurement window to stay re-derivable for
at least as long as the records that quote it, so a committed record can be
re-checked by a later session instead of being taken on trust.

## Options (not a decision — intake should choose)

1. **Raise `logging.retention_days`** (e.g. 7→14 or 30). Cheap in disk: measured
   on 2026-11-05, `/var/log/llama-proxy` holds 46 `proxy.log*.gz` archives
   totalling **42 MB** (≈0.9 MB per six-hour segment), so doubling or
   quadrupling retention costs tens of MB, not GB. The knob already exists
   (`logging.retention_days`). Costs: more files in one directory (check
   `prune_logs` startup scan time) and the logrotate drop-in's `rotate 7`
   safety net must be raised to match, or it will prune what the in-process
   handler retains.
2. **Archive the window's archives with the record** — a `--emit-archives`
   mode or a documented `tar`/`rsync` step alongside a record commit. Larger
   repo footprint (or an external artefact store), but makes the record
   self-contained forever.
3. **Record the harness output as the artefact of authority** and drop the
   "regenerates byte-for-byte" expectation from records older than retention —
   documentation-only, no code change; what `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` does today.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, for intake)

- AC1: A documented retention window is at least as long as the longest-lived
  measurement record the project commits, with the value stated in
  `docs/dev/` and pinned by a test.
- AC2: A measurement record older than the retention window is either
  reproducible from a committed/archived artefact, or the record states its
  provenance classes explicitly (no silent re-derivation claim).
- AC3: Disk cost of the chosen retention is measured, not assumed, and stated
  on the host-install/retention doc.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md`
  ("Provenance and coverage") — the coverage map and the pruning mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` (`setup_logging`, `prune_logs`,
  `logging.retention_days` default 7).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` (`rotate 7`, `size`-free daily safety net).
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/decompression discovery (unaffected;
  the loss is retention, not discovery).

## Goal

Produce a **proposal** (no implementation without explicit producer approval) for separating audit/bulk traffic from interactive user traffic at the shared local gate.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I. Rec 5 of the root-cause analysis. **This item must not change code, config or the running proxy.**

## Why it matters (measured, certified window 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00)

- **20 of the 60** `prefill_deadline` events are audit sessions (`audit-*`), with 44k–103k prompts; 11 audit events are attributed capacity and 9 predicted-warmth.
- Audit is excluded from the (b2) user-class criterion, **but not from its cause**: audit prefills occupy the shared gate and the second slot, and the measured cold rate swings **235–295 tok/s (contended) vs 530–770 tok/s (best case)**.
- Audits raise the occupancy class (9/60, 15 %, and under-counted while `/slots` times out), i.e. they make *user* events miss even though their own events are not counted.

## Scope

**In:** a written proposal in `docs/dev/` (or an appendix to the existing prefill/admission docs) covering options, costs and the decision criteria.

**Out:** any implementation, config change, deployment or proxy restart. Implementation happens only in a follow-up item created **after** producer approval.

## Options the proposal must cost

1. **Audit remote-only** (or audit-on-a-different-provider): zero local audit load; cost = remote tokens/latency.
2. **Idle-gated local access for audits**: local only when the pool has been idle ≥ N s; needs a measured N.
3. **Priority-weighted gate**: user `high`/`medium` pre-empts queued audit prefills; needs the priority plumbing already present (LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI).
4. **Per-class deadline**: audits get a shorter local deadline (e.g. 60 s) and fall back sooner.
5. **Do nothing** — with the measured cost stated.

For each: expected effect on the user-class rate, on local coverage/utilisation, on remote spend, and the risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proposal written.** A document states each option, its mechanism, the measured evidence it rests on, expected effect on the user-class combined rate (baseline 2.223/h; target ≤ 0.5/h), local coverage, and remote cost. It names a recommendation and the decision criteria.
- **AC2 — No implementation.** The item changes **no** source, config or runtime state; git diff is empty apart from the proposal document (or the doc lives in the work item description if a doc is premature). No proxy restart is performed by this item.
- **AC3 — Impact model reproducible.** The projected numbers come from a stated, reproducible computation over the certified window dataset (`/tmp/ac3-window-2026-11-06.json`, recorded on LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) — e.g. "remove audit events → X user events remain, Y/h", with the command/analysis recorded.
- **AC4 — Producer approval gate.** `needsProducerReview` is set on creation; the item advances only when the producer records approval (a comment naming the chosen option). Until then it stays `idea`/`intake_complete` and dispatchable-for-proposal only.
- **AC5 — Follow-up on approval.** On approval, create the implementation item (issue type `feature`, high) carrying: the restart AC (proxy restarted via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` with PID/HEAD/`/health` evidence), the dated-title re-anchor AC, and the impact measurement. Link it here with `related`/`depends-on` as appropriate.
- **AC6 — Proxy restart AC (deferred, not waived).** This item performs no restart. The restart it is accountable for is the one in the approved follow-up: that follow-up must restart the proxy and record old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD and `/health` before its impact measurement. If the producer rejects the proposal, state explicitly that no restart is owed and close.
- **AC7 — Dated titles.** The dated-title re-anchor (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` in open titles) is owed by the approved follow-up's restart; this item records that obligation and, on rejection, notes that no re-anchor is triggered.

## Relationship

- Related: LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (serialise audits at the shared local resource), LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI (batch work must send a priority header so interactive sessions are protected), LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 (early-released local dispatch starvation).
- The producer's (b2) re-scope conversation (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) should consider this proposal as one of the levers.

## Earliest date/time for implementation

**2026-11-07T14:16Z** — the measurement window anchor plus 24 h.

Per the shared convention in [`docs/dev/measurement-windows.md`](docs/dev/measurement-windows.md) (LP-0MVWC0FAT0018PMW):

- **Window anchor** = the proxy restart that loaded the rung. That is the running process
  (`.venv/bin/python3 -m uvicorn proxy.server:app`, pid 2634864, `ps -o lstart` **2026-11-06T14:15:50Z**, log line
  `2026-11-06 14:15:50`). Independent confirmation that this start loaded the rung: the interpreter compiled
  `proxy/proxy/__pycache__/provider.cpython-312.pyc` at **14:15:52** and that bytecode contains the
  `local_last_resort*` symbols; the rung had merged to `dev` as `52130e54d` on 2026-11-05 05:48, ~32 h earlier.
- **Window start** = the first whole minute after that restart → **2026-11-06T14:16Z**.
- **Earliest the window can close** = window start + 24 h → **2026-11-07T14:16Z**.

That instant has passed (the same anchor already serves LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K, LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8 and
LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q, all of which quote `2026-11-06T14:16Z → 2026-11-07T14:16Z`), so this item is actionable
immediately — the date above is a floor, not a start signal.

Two further constraints:

- **The window must be restart-free.** A restart inside it (`start-proxy.sh --restart`, a deploy, a crash
  recovery) re-anchors it: a partial window never yields a PASS. Confirm with `ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid
  and by grepping the window's logs for `Starting LLama Proxy Server`. Coordinate with the shared calendar
  before any deploy.
- **Act before ≈ 2026-11-13.** `logging.retention_days` is 7 (`proxy/config.yaml`), so the post-deploy segments
  (`proxy.log.2026-11-07_*`, `proxy.log.2026-11-08_*`) are pruned roughly 7 days after the deploy. Past that
  the window must be re-based on a fresh deploy (`docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md` covers archiving
  the raw segments first).

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want the ≥ 24 h post-deploy evaluation of the last-resort local admission rung (AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W) performed and recorded, so that the rung is either confirmed to reduce `All providers exhausted` failures inside idle gaps without a regression in prefill evictions/discarded tokens, or is killed/retuned with the measured evidence.

## Why this is a separate item

AC8 of LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W is a *post-deploy* criterion: it cannot be satisfied by code, tests or documentation, only by a measurement window taken after the rung has been running in production. The implementation item delivered the rung, the tests and the measurement surfaces (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` → "Last-resort rung (LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W): the post-deploy measurement"); the actual window belongs here.

Baseline to beat (measured 2026-10-29 23:43:30 → 2026-10-30 23:43:30, *before* the rung existed):

- 236 of the window's 686 `All providers exhausted` warnings (34%) occurred inside 13 GPU-idle gaps carrying 98 inbound requests and 0 streams.
- The idle-admit ladder fired 1,337 times and refused 1,291 (96.6%) on `prefill_budget_exceeded`; 292,924 prefill tokens / 44 evictions discarded per 24 h.

## In scope

- Run the usage analysis over a ≥ 24 h window that lies entirely after the deployment instant, e.g.
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-11-06 14:16:00" --end "2026-11-07 14:16:00"` (the CLI supports arbitrary `--start`/`--end`), and repeat for a later restart-free window if the first is inconclusive.
- Attribute every `local_last_resort_admit` line (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `threshold_seconds`, `deadline_s`, `warm_cap`, `remote_exhausted=true`, `session`, `turn`) and every `routing_idle_admit_refused` it superseded.
- Read the three comparison surfaces from the same window: `All providers exhausted` inside idle gaps vs the 236 baseline, `local_evictions_after_acceptance` with `reason=prefill_deadline`, and discarded prefill tokens.
- Record the numbers, the window boundaries, the exact commands and the verdict on this item, and bring the result back to LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W (comment, and re-audit that item so its AC8 — now scoped to this handover — stays consistent with the measured outcome).

## Out of scope

- Any code change. If the evaluation shows `local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low (rising `prefill_deadline` evictions), the fix is a raised knob value, filed as its own item; if it shows no benefit, the fix is the kill switch (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`), also its own item.
- Re-measuring remote provider quota/capacity root causes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A restart-free ≥ 24 h window lying entirely after the window start (2026-11-06T14:16Z) is analysed with the deterministic CLI, and the window boundaries, the restart-free evidence (`ps -o lstart` on the uvicorn pid, no `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker inside the window) and the exact command are recorded on this item.
- AC2: The window's `All providers exhausted` count inside GPU-idle gaps is reported against the 236/686 baseline, with the idle-gap definition and the gap count stated.
- AC3: `local_last_resort_admit` lines in the window are counted and attributed (per-session/per-turn) with their `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `idle_seconds`, `deadline_s` distribution; if the count is zero, the reason is stated (remote chain never empty, prompt above warm cap, or GPU not idle) with the supporting log evidence.
- AC4: `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (`reason=prefill_deadline`) and discarded prefill tokens are reported for the window and compared with the pre-rung 24 h figures (44 evictions / 292,924 discarded prefill tokens).
- AC5: An explicit verdict — **keep** (exhaustions inside idle gaps fell, neither eviction metric rose), **retune** (`local_last_resort_deadline_seconds` too low — quote the distribution) or **kill** (`local_last_resort_idle_seconds: 0`) — recorded on this item with the numbers that justify it, and echoed as a comment on LP-0MVWAMY8M001KE4W.

# Usage report: per-model provider status table with next-check time

## Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator reading the daily usage report, I want a table immediately
after the performance-metrics scorecard showing the **current routing status of
every provider entry in every model chain, and when that status will next be
checked or re-evaluated**, so that a silently deadlocked provider is visible in
the report the morning it happens instead of being found by hand weeks later.

## Problem

The report can say *how often* the chain fell back and to where, but it cannot
answer the question the operator actually asks when fallback is high: **"which
provider is unavailable right now, why, and when does that change?"** The
statuses that suppress a provider are already computed by the resolver but
never surfaced:

| Gate (evaluated in this order, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`) | Line | Suppresses the entry for |
|---|---|---|
| `usage_limit_account` (same account already exhausted this request) | ~11533 | the rest of that request |
| `quota_exhausted` / `dispatch_on_balance` (proactive quota snapshot) | ~11546 | until the blocking quota window resets |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (persisted account quarantine) | ~11560 | until `reset_at` (minutes → **weeks**) |
| `quota_hard_stop` | ~11606 | until the monthly window resets |
| `provider_cooldown` | ~11628 | 30 s – 300 s |
| `outside its available_times` | ~11647 | until the next window edge |

The gap is not theoretical. On 2026-11-12 05:46:05 `opencode-go` returned HTTP
402 `Insufficient balance`; the proxy recorded a `balance_exhaustion`
quarantine bounded by the **monthly plan** reset — **2026-11-23 08:45:55** —
and then skipped the entry on every request for eleven days. Nothing in the
report showed it: every nightly run looked normal, the account simply never
appeared, and the deadlock was only found by reading `proxy-state.json` by
hand and grepping `usage_limit_reset_pending` out of the live log. A single
table with `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | next checked
2026-11-23 08:45` would have made it obvious on the first morning.

Visibility is also the cheaper alternative to automating early quarantine
release: the operator can see that a top-up will not be picked up until the
plan window rolls over, and act (or not) deliberately.

## Scope

In scope (usage-report skill only — `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`):

- a new `## Provider status` table rendered **immediately after** the
  `## Performance metrics summary` scorecard table (`scripts/reporting.py`,
  currently line ~1384) and **before** `## Performance metric details`
  (line ~1481);
- a new deterministic module (suggested `scripts/provider_status.py`) that
  derives the rows; it must not re-implement the resolver's gate semantics —
  see *Design notes*;
- an additive `--json` block (`provider_status`);
- tests (unit + fixture-rendered) and the skill's `SKILL.md` / `REFERENCE.md`
  updates.

Out of scope:

- changing any proxy routing behaviour, quarantine duration or probe cadence
  (this item is observational only — it must not alter what the proxy does);
- adding a network call to the proxy, Prometheus or any other live service;
- alerting/paging on status (the report row is the deliverable).

## Table shape

One table, ordered by model chain (config order) then by chain position, so
each model's fallback sequence reads top-down:

| Model | # | Provider entry | Status | Detail | Next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plan | 1 | local-qwen3 | eligible | — | next request |
| plan | 2 | opencode-go-3 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 10.3 h | 2026-11-17 10:07 |
| plan | 3 | opencode-go-2 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 13 days | 2026-11-30 00:05 |
| plan | 4 | opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | balance exhaustion, window unknown | 2026-11-23 08:45 |
| plan | 5 | munitoai-free | usage_limit_reset_pending | window unknown | 2026-11-17 00:02 |
| plan | 6 | munitoai | outside available_times | next window 10:00–23:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |
| plan | 7 | deepseek-flash | outside available_times | next window 10:00–00:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |

`Status` is the **first suppressing gate** the resolver would hit (the order
above), or `eligible` when none does. `Detail` carries the gate's own evidence
(quota window + percent, quarantine window + reason, cooldown key and
remaining seconds, or the window being waited for). `Next check` is the
instant the suppression is expected to lift, or the next point at which the
proxy will re-evaluate it — defined in the next section so the column is never
ambiguous.

An `Events in window` column (skip count per entry, derived from the existing
`Skipping provider=` parse) is optional; add it only if it costs no extra log
pass.

## Semantics of `Next check`

The column must state *how* it was derived, because three different mechanisms
answer "when next":

| Status | `Next check` | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `eligible` | `next request` | the resolver's gate checks run per request; nothing is pending |
| `provider_cooldown` | cooldown expiry instant | `provider_unavailable_until` in the provider state file |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (hard / window-derived) | quarantine `reset_at` | `usage_reset_at` in the state file; revalidated from the next quota poll, so the instant is the *earliest* lift, not a guarantee |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (soft / guessed) | `now + min(probe interval, reset_at)` | the self-healing probe cadence (`_USAGE_LIMIT_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 300 s) is what actually re-checks these |
| `quota_exhausted` / `quota_hard_stop` | the blocking window's `resetsAt` | the last `quota poll ok` line for that account (`seconds_to_reset`) |
| `outside available_times` | the next window edge in UTC | `available_times` from `proxy/config.yaml`, including overnight wraparound (e.g. `22:00-02:00`) |
| any status with no usable evidence | `unknown` | never a fabricated instant |

## Design notes and assumptions

**Data sources (all local files / already-parsed log lines — no network call):**

1. `proxy/config.yaml` — the model chains, entry order, `available_times`,
   `use_balance`, `api_key_env`, `quota_poll_interval_seconds`.
2. `proxy/provider-state.json` — `provider_unavailable_until` (cooldowns) and
   `usage_reset_at` (account quarantines). Path is overridable by
   `LLAMA_PROXY_PROVIDER_STATE_FILE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:296`); the
   analyser must honour that environment variable and treat a missing file as
   "no pending suppression", not an error.
3. The **last** `quota poll ok account=...` line in the analysis window per
   account — the only persisted view of the in-process quota snapshot. Poll
   cadence is `quota_poll_interval_seconds` (900 s), so a window shorter than
   that may legitimately have none.

**Single source of truth (hard requirement).** The gate order and the
reason strings must not be duplicated as prose in the report module. Either
import the constants from `proxy/provider.py` (the skill already imports
`MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON` this way — see the capacity-signals section of
`SKILL.md`, including the PEP 420 namespace-package caveat it documents), or
add a small canonical `GATE_ORDER` tuple there that both the resolver and the
analyser consume. A test must fail if the two orders diverge.

**Assumption A1 — row granularity.** "Each model" is read as *each model chain
(`plan`, `author`, `code`, …) × each provider entry in it*, because the entry
is the unit the gates act on and the chain position is what makes a dead entry
fatal. `opencode-go` therefore appears once per chain it belongs to. If the
operator prefers one row per distinct entry with a `Model chains` column
instead, that is a rendering change only — the derivation is identical.

**Assumption A2 — reference instant.** All relative figures are computed
against the report window's end (the analysis `--end`, default now), stated in
the section's intro sentence, so a re-run over an old window reproduces the
same table rather than silently using wall-clock time.

**Assumption A3 — live-state caveat.** `provider-state.json` and the last
quota poll are point-in-time snapshots, not window aggregates. The section
intro must say so in one sentence: the table describes the state at report
generation, not the state during the window. This is the same honesty
discipline the report already applies to the GPU row and the engine
cross-check.

**Assumption A4 — local entries.** `local-qwen3` has no endpoint and no quota
account. It is rendered with `eligible` and `next request`, or with the
existing local-route cooldown reason when one is recorded — it must not be
dropped from the table, because a reader comparing chains needs the whole
sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `report.md` contains `## Provider status` immediately after the
  `## Performance metrics summary` table and before `## Performance metric
  details`. A test asserts the section order, not just presence.
- **AC2** — The table has one row per (model chain, provider entry) in
  `proxy/config.yaml` order and chain order, and a test asserts the row count
  and order equal the config's for a fixture config.
- **AC3** — `Status` is the *first* suppressing gate in the resolver's order;
  a unit test covers an entry suppressed by two mechanisms simultaneously
  (e.g. `usage_limit_reset_pending` and `provider_cooldown`) and asserts the
  earlier gate wins.
- **AC4** — `Next check` is derived per the semantics table, with unit tests
  for: cooldown expiry, hard quarantine `reset_at`, soft/guessed quarantine
  capped at the probe interval, quota window reset from the last
  `quota poll ok` line, an `available_times` window later the same UTC day,
  and an overnight window that wraps past midnight.
- **AC5** — The reproduction from this item's *Problem* section renders as
  `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | 2026-11-23 08:45` from a fixture
  built on the 2026-11-12 state file — i.e. the incident is visible.
- **AC6** — Degradation is named, never fabricated: with a missing state file,
  no `quota poll ok` line, an unparseable `available_times` entry, or an
  unknown status string, the cell reads `unknown` and the run still exits 0.
  A test covers each of the four.
- **AC7** — `--json` carries an additive `provider_status` block with the same
  rows (`model`, `position`, `entry`, `status`, `detail`, `next_check`,
  `next_check_basis`) and no existing key changes. A test asserts the Markdown
  table and the JSON rows agree.
- **AC8** — Gate order and reason strings have a single source of truth: a
  test fails if `provider_status`'s gate order or a reason string diverges from
  the proxy resolver's.
- **AC9** — No network call is added: a test asserts the module performs no
  HTTP request (the skill's `tests/conftest.py` network seam already blocks one,
  so the test proves it is never attempted) and the 05:00 cron line is
  unchanged.
- **AC10** — An empty window (no logs) still renders a valid table from config
  + state alone, with `unknown` where log evidence is needed, and the 05:00
  cron exits 0.
- **AC11** — `SKILL.md` gains a `## Provider status` section (what the columns
  mean, the `Next check` semantics table, the live-state caveat) and
  `REFERENCE.md` documents the data sources and the `--json` schema; both are
  reviewed against the rendered output in the same change.
- **AC12** — No proxy behaviour change: the diff touches only
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (plus, at most, one extracted constant in
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` for AC8) and the full test suite passes.

## Problem statement

The first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll after a proxy restart can fire
*before* child-port discovery has succeeded, so it takes the router-port
fallback path: it logs a `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING
(`model=Qwen3`, `source=log_signal`), increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
and traverses the router (`:8080`) instead of the model child port.

Consequence: every 24 h post-restart verification window on this surface
starts with a guaranteed chat-model fallback, which fails a zero-tolerance
"chat-model fallback delta == 0" acceptance criterion even when
steady-state operation is clean.

## Evidence (measured, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window 2026-11-16T15:20:47Z → 2026-11-17T15:20:47Z)

The window is anchored to the proxy restart (`pid 3720326`, `lstart`
2026-11-16T15:20:47Z), so the process-lifetime counter delta *is* the window
delta. In `proxy.log.2026-11-16_15`, immediately after the boot sequence
(`Started TTS server`, `death capture: armed`, `Slot occupancy sampler
started (interval 10.0s)`):

```text
2026-11-16 15:20:51,411 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model child port discovered for model=Qwen3 (source=log_signal); falling back to router port 8080 — every proxy-initiated /slots poll will traverse t...
2026-11-16 15:20:51,435 - WARNING - llama-server --version returned 127
2026-11-16 15:20:51,560 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

- Only **one** `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker in the whole window
  (15:20:49.786, the anchor process's own boot) ⇒ no in-window restart.
- `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  = **1.0** for a process that started at the window start.
- Exactly **one** `slots_child_port_unavailable` line in the window, at
  window start **+4.4 s**; **zero** for the remaining 23 h 59 m 56 s.
- The same transient is visible in the earlier LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 window
  (3 × `model=Qwen3`, each one within 3 s of a restart) — i.e. it is
  restart-correlated, not busy-child-correlated.

## Desired change

Make the boot-time slot poll child-port-aware: either

1. retry/defer the first slot poll until child-port discovery has resolved
   (bounded backoff), or
2. mark the poll as a boot transient so the fallback counter / WARNING are
   not incremented before discovery has had a chance to succeed.

The zero-tolerance signal (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` + the
`slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING) must stay usable as a *regression*
signal — a boot-time increment makes a clean 24 h window indistinguishable
from one real discovery regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After a proxy restart, the first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll
  does not increment `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and does not emit `slots_child_port_unavailable` when the model child port
  becomes discoverable within the boot window.
- **AC2** — A genuine discovery regression (child port never discoverable)
  still increments the counter and emits the WARNING; covered by a test.
- **AC3** — Reproduced by a test: boot sequence with a not-yet-ready child
  port ⇒ no fallback counter increment; child port never ready ⇒ counter
  increments once per throttled interval.
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
- **AC5** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A restarted proxy no longer looks like it had a child-port discovery
regression on its very first slot poll, so a clean 24 h window can pass the
zero-tolerance fallback check.
data.title: Boot-time chat-model child-port fallback: the first slot poll after a proxy restart falls back to the router (Qwen3, slots_child_port_unavailable)

## Summary

Separate the per-request fixed overhead from the per-token cached rate by adding a `base_prefill_ms` (intercept) coefficient to the per-bucket regression, so a 99 %-cached follow-up is priced at its near-instant cached service plus one small fixed overhead instead of inheriting a cold-rate `coded_ms_per_token` pushed to the `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN` clamp.

## Target outcome

`estimate_prefill_seconds` for the pinned 7.9 k / 99 %-cached / 49-new-token prompt drops from 22.6 s to under 5 s, the cached coefficient no longer absorbs fixed overhead, and cold/percentile pricing is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_fit()` solves a three-coefficient model `eta_ms = base_prefill_ms + coded_tokens*coded_ms_per_token + new_tokens*prefill_ms_per_token` from the same rolling window, with a documented degenerate-window fallback to the existing two-coefficient fit (unidentifiable intercept keeps a sane default, never a fabricated 0).
- `Coefficients` and `AdmissionDecision` carry `base_prefill_ms`, and `estimate_prefill_seconds` / `projected_wait_seconds` include it; the pinned warm case prices below 5 s and a `cached_ratio == 1.0`, `new_tokens == 0` prompt prices at the fixed-overhead bound only (parent AC1, AC2).
- `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN` is reconsidered and revised with the warm-sample evidence, `MIN_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN` still bounds the cached rate from below, and the cached coefficient is clamped to the revised range (parent AC2).
- The percentile-uplift path (`eta_percentile > 0` and `prompt_tokens >= eta_percentile_min_tokens`) applies to the token terms only and never inflates the fixed overhead, so a warm prompt at the percentile floor is not re-inflated (parent constraints, AC5).
- Conservative percentile pricing for cold prompts >= 20 k tokens (`LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN`) is unchanged: its regression tests stay green, and the cold ETA for a 25 k cold prompt is not reduced (parent AC5).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `_solve` to a 3×3 normal-equation solve; return `None` (or a two-term solve) when the intercept is not identifiable from the window.
- Add `DEFAULT_BASE_PREFILL_MS`, `MIN_BASE_PREFILL_MS`, `MAX_BASE_PREFILL_MS` next to the existing clamp constants, with the conservatism factor applied consistently.
- Thread `base_prefill_ms` through `Coefficients`, `_fit_coefficients_from_samples`, `_fit` call sites and `estimate_prefill_seconds`.
- Adjust the uplift block so `pred_ref_ms` and the scaled terms include the intercept consistently (scale token terms, add the intercept once).
- Keep the cold-only window selection and contended-bucket selection untouched; only the interior fit changes.

## Constraints

- No new configuration knob is required; the revised ceiling stays a documented module constant (revisit only if live evidence demands it).
- Must not change window selection, bucket boundaries, percentile floor or `local_admission_guard_*` settings.
- Fail-open behaviour on uncalibrated buckets is preserved byte-for-byte.

## Risky assumptions

- Three coefficients are identifiable from a window of ≥ 5 samples with mixed cache states; if not, the degenerate fallback keeps today's numbers and the warm case stays mis-priced — the sibling test item makes that failure visible.
- The fixed overhead is genuinely per-request (hundreds of ms), not a per-token effect; the measured 436 ms first byte for 49 new tokens supports this, but a live re-measure is the confirmation.

## Dependencies

- No blocking prerequisite; the warm-calibration test item asserts the target numbers and follows this item.

## Deliverables

- Intercept-capable fit in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` with documented constants and revised `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN`.
- Comment on the parent recording the fitted coefficients and eta before/after for the pinned case.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `_fit`, `_fit_coefficients_from_samples`, `_solve`, `Coefficients`, `estimate_prefill_seconds`, clamp constants, uplift path
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` — existing fit invariants to keep green
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — cold/percentile rows that must not regress
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_cold_fit.py` — cold-window fit rows that must not regress

## Goal

Land the synthetic-log fixtures and failing tests that define the eviction-attribution split and the `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table, so the parent's AC1 and AC2 implementation is driven by tests rather than written first and characterised afterwards. ## Context

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` already parses llama-server logs (prompts, prompt tokens requested/reused/prefilled, full prefills small/large, evictions and their sizes, cache-state samples, checkpoint sizes) and `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py` drives it from inline synthetic corpora written to a temp dir. ## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic corpus exercises the eviction-attribution join: an eviction line for a known entry size, followed within the match window by a full prefill of a prompt whose token count matches the evicted entry, and the test asserts the prefill is classified as eviction-attributable.
- Tests cover the conservative cases and assert each classification: no preceding eviction -> genuinely new tokens; prefill outside the match window -> not attributed; prefill whose size differs beyond the stated tolerance -> not attributed; a `forcing full prompt re-processing` task -> classified by the same rule, not by the message.

- The red run is recorded in a work-item comment (`/skill:test` changed-scope run) before implementation begins.

## Goal

Make `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` attribute a full prefill either to an eviction (a prefix that was previously cached and then lost) or to genuinely new work, then run it over a named surviving window and commit the artifact that becomes the before/baseline measurement for this item.

## Context

The 2026-11-03 incident corpus referenced by the parent item has rotated away: `/var/log/llama-proxy/` retains daily files from 2026-11-04 (near-empty, 922 B) onward, with real content from 2026-11-07. Measured on 2026-11-18, the surviving saturated windows are *busier* than the incident: cache-state maxima of 26 prompts (11-07), 27 (11-08), 29 (11-10), 31 (11-11 and `llama-server.2.log`) and 47 prompts (11-13). The baseline therefore becomes the nearest surviving saturated window, with the substitution and the corpus file list recorded in the artifact's `meta` block — exactly the fallback the parent item's risks section already allows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Attribution is measured, not assumed — over a fixed, named window a reproducible measurement (committed script or artifact) decomposes prefilled prompt tokens into (a) genuinely new tokens, where the prompt or prefix was never cached (new session or genuine divergence), and (b) re-prefills of a prefix that was previously cached and then lost, reporting the eviction-attributable share and token volume; the attribution method, its match rule and its error bounds or limitations are stated alongside the numbers.
- The match rule is explicit and conservative: an evicted entry (size in MiB, and its token count derived from the measured checkpoint term) is matched to a later full prefill only inside a bounded task-index window and a stated size tolerance; anything unmatched is classified as genuinely new work, never as eviction-attributable, and the count of unmatched candidates is reported so the conservatism is visible.
- The four token buckets (eviction-attributable, genuinely new, unattributed remainder, reused) reconcile to the reported prefilled total, and the script exits non-zero or prints an explicit warning if they do not.
- A committed artifact `docs/dev/prompt-cache-attribution-2026-11-1x.json` records the corpus file list, the window, the match rule and tolerance in `meta`, the attribution figures, and a one-line note that the 2026-11-03 window is unavailable and this is the nearest surviving substitute.
- Attribution is cross-checked against the proxy's per-dispatch `cached_ratio` where a proxy log corpus for the same window is available, and the cross-check result (agree / disagree / not available) is recorded rather than assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend the parser state with a bounded list of evicted entries (`size MiB`, derived token count, task index at eviction), captured from the existing `cache size limit reached, removing oldest entry` lines.
2. Classify each full prefill as attributed/genuinely new inside `_finalise`, reusing the existing `large_tokens` threshold and full-prefill detection rather than adding a parallel path.
3. Add summary fields (`eviction_attributed_*`, `genuinely_new_tokens_prefilled`, `unattributed_full_prefills`, `attribution_reconciles`) and a rendered attribution section; add `--attribution-window` and `--attribution-tolerance` flags with documented defaults.
4. State the rule, the tolerance and the error bounds in the module docstring and in the rendered output; keep the existing metric contract unchanged so current artifacts stay comparable.
5. Select the baseline window, run the measurement, commit the artifact, and record the exact command in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`.

Implementation slice for parent AC2 (a trade-off table supports the recommendation).

## Goal

Produce, from the AC1 measurement, a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table and derive the recommended pair from it, naming the `MemAvailable` floor at which an increase must be refused — so the two knobs are decided together from one measured table instead of from a per-prompt constant inherited from the 16-prompt era.

## Context

`recommend()` currently proposes a `cache-ram` only: it reports the checkpoint term but never varies it, and it keeps `ctx-checkpoints` fixed because "fewer checkpoints can itself increase full prefills". The 2026-11-03 incident (26 retained prompts, 39,829 of 40,960 MiB) and the surviving corpora (up to 47 retained prompts) show the prompt count is the term that moved, so both knobs must appear in one table with their costs side by side. The host is 128 GiB unified memory with the documented reserve `max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)` = 12,743.7 MiB.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A trade-off table supports the recommendation — the measurement produces a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table stating, per candidate configuration: prompts held, per-prompt state, the checkpoint term, killed prompts (prompts that would no longer fit), the checkpoint resume value (rollback granularity and the full-prefill risk of having fewer anchors), and MiB per prompt; the recommended pair is derived from that table and names the MemAvailable floor at which an increase must be refused.
- Candidates are concrete and finite: at least `ctx-checkpoints` in {32, 16, 8} x `cache-ram` in {current 40,960 MiB, the measured requirement at the observed prompt maximum, and the same capacity reached with a halved checkpoint term}, plus any value already adopted by `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51` if that item has landed.
- "Killed prompts" is defined and computed: the number of observed retained prompts that would no longer fit at that candidate, i.e. `cache_ram / per_prompt` subtracted from the measured prompt maximum, floored at zero.
- The resume value is stated qualitatively per checkpoint count (rollback granularity in tokens at the observed context, and the risk that fewer anchors means less chance of matching a reused prefix, so more full prefills), with the measured checkpoint size in MiB per checkpoint.
- The headroom verdict states which form of the invariant it uses — pre-allocation (`MemAvailable - cache-ram >= reserve`) or resident delta (only the increase must be available when the cache is already resident) — and reports both, because the two give different verdicts today; the recommended pair names the `MemAvailable` floor value in MiB that refuses a further increase.
- The table is rendered as markdown for the tuning doc and emitted in the JSON artifact, and the recommendation names the row it came from.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Refactor `recommend()` so the per-prompt and checkpoint arithmetic is a pure function of `(cache_ram, ctx_checkpoints, measured inputs)`, keeping the current single-value output backward compatible.
2. Add a `tradeoff_table(summary, ...)` builder over the finite candidate set, returning rows plus the floor verdict.
3. Add a `--tradeoff` CLI mode that prints the markdown table and includes it in `--json`; keep `--recommend` behaviour unchanged for existing reproduction commands.
4. Record the derived pair and the floor in the artifact for the same window as the AC1 measurement, then hand the values to the apply-and-pin slice.

## Definition of Done

Table committed in the artifact and reproduced in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`; `/skill:test` changed-scope run green; build -> changed-scope tests -> commit order respected.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`
- `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py`
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-attribution-2026-11-13.json`
- `proxy/proxy/host_pressure.py`

## Dependencies

Blocked by the attribution slice (the table consumes its per-prompt and attribution figures). Blocks the apply-and-pin slice.

## Parent AC traceability

Parent AC2 — the trade-off table, the recommended pair derived from it, and the named `MemAvailable` floor.

Verification slice for parent AC4 (post-change verification, deployed), AC5 (no throughput or latency regression), AC6 (documentation) and AC7 (full suite).

## Goal

Deploy the chosen geometry, confirm the running child carries it, and prove on a comparable window that eviction-attributable re-prefill and prefilled tokens per request fell without regressing prompt-eval throughput or client-visible first-byte latency — or record that they did not, with the reason.

## Context

Deploy is `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (detached by default, health-polled); killing the proxy is never acceptable. The restart replaces llama-server, so any request in flight at that moment fails: run it between tool calls with `/health` polled to healthy, and expect the cache to start empty, so the post-change window begins at the restart. Sessions served by the Local Proxy lose their connection only if they dispatch during the restart, which is why the deploy is its own slice rather than a step inside another change.

Baseline comparison is request-matched, not calendar-matched: the AC1 baseline artifact records the corpus file list, so the post-change window must be selected to a comparable request count and reported with `requests` alongside every per-request figure. The prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio is workload-dependent and must be reported with that caveat, never as the sole evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Post-change verification, deployed — the change is deployed with `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never by killing the proxy) and the spawned Qwen3 child is confirmed to carry the new flags; a post-change measurement over a window comparable to the AC1 baseline shows both the eviction-attributable re-prefill share and prefilled prompt tokens per request falling measurably, with the prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio recorded alongside its workload caveat.
- The spawned child's arguments are confirmed from the live process (`ps`/`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) to carry the new `--cache-ram` and `--ctx-checkpoints` values, reconciled against `models.ini`, and the confirmation is recorded with the timestamp and the child pid.
- No throughput or latency regression — prompt-eval throughput and client-visible first-byte latency measured over the same before/after windows do not regress, or any movement is attributed with evidence to a named confounder rather than to this change.
- The before/after table records per-request metrics (eviction-attributable prefills per request, prefilled tokens per request, evictions per request, first-byte median/p90, prompt-eval tokens/s) with the request count of each window, and a "Comparability" note stating how the windows were matched.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes — a `/skill:test` full run recorded on the final commit.
- A committed post-change artifact `docs/dev/prompt-cache-attribution-<window>-postchange.json` and a verification section in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` carry the numbers, the command lines and the corpus file lists for both windows.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Deploy with `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, poll `/health` until `status: healthy` with `llama_server_running: true`, then confirm the child's flags.
2. Run the attribution measurement over the post-change corpus once it reaches a comparable request count; commit the artifact with its `meta` block.
3. Build the before/after table and the Comparability note; attribute any throughput or latency movement explicitly.
4. Update the tuning doc verification section and the README/docs-site references; run the full suite.

## Definition of Done

Post-change artifact and verification section committed; `/skill:test` full run green on the final commit; the deploy timestamp, child pid and confirmed flags recorded in a work-item comment; build -> tests -> commit order respected.

Parent: LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR (priority header trust gate)

Implement the trusted-source IP allowlist module that makes the test-first suite from LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR child 1 pass.

## Scope

New module `proxy/proxy/priority_trust.py`, stdlib only (`ipaddress`, `logging`). No new dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `priority_trust_config(server_config)` returns `{"enabled": bool, "networks": tuple}`: `enabled` from `server.priority_trust.enabled` (default `False`), `networks` parsed from `server.priority_trust.allowed_sources` (default empty). A bare address is accepted as a host prefix (`127.0.0.1` → `/32`, `::1` → `/128`). Malformed entries are logged at `WARNING` and skipped; a non-dict section or non-list `allowed_sources` degrades to the defaults.
2. **Configurable gate.** `server.priority_trust` is accepted with `enabled` (bool, default `false`) and `allowed_sources` (list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR blocks, default empty). With the gate disabled, every client's declared priority is honoured exactly as today.
3. `is_trusted_source(source_ip, server_config)` returns `True` when the gate is disabled, `False` for `None`/empty/unparsable addresses, and otherwise evaluates `ipaddress.ip_address(source_ip) in network` membership across the parsed networks (IPv4 and IPv6 both supported). It never raises — a bad `source_ip` is a returned `False`, not an exception.
4. `apply_trust_gate(source_ip, declared_priority, server_config)` returns the declared priority unchanged unless the gate is enabled, the source is untrusted and the declared priority ranks above `medium`; in that case it returns `medium`. Reuse `proxy.priority.parse_priority` / `PRIORITY_RANK` rather than re-deriving the vocabulary (no duplicate priority tables).
5. **Restriction above medium.** With the gate enabled, a source whose peer address matches `allowed_sources` may claim `low|medium|high`; a source that does not match has its declared priority reduced to `medium` whenever it is above `medium` (i.e. `high`). Declared `low` and `medium` are never altered.
6. **Silent downgrade, logged once.** A downgraded request is served normally — no 4xx/5xx, no `Retry-After`, no dropped connection — and each decision is logged once at `INFO` with the peer address, the declared priority and the verdict. Exactly one `INFO` record per gate decision (`priority_trust: source=%s declared=%s verdict=%s`, verdict `allowed` or `downgraded_to_medium`); no log line when the gate is disabled.
7. **Deny-by-default when enabled.** Gate enabled with an empty `allowed_sources` means no source is trusted (every `high` claim downgrades); gate disabled means every source is trusted. An invalid address/CIDR entry is ignored with a warning rather than crashing routing.
8. Module docstring states the trust model: the allowlist is evaluated against the direct socket peer only; `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` are deliberately not consulted because a client can set them.
9. `proxy/tests/test_priority_trust.py` unit tests for config/matching/gate pass; existing `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` remains green.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/priority_trust.py` — new module
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — imported for `parse_priority` / `PRIORITY_RANK` only (no behavioural change in this child)
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_trust.py` — the suite this child turns green

Parent: LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR (priority header trust gate)

Wire the gate into the live priority computation so an untrusted `X-Priority: high` is silently downgraded to `medium` before the cheap-window cap.

## Scope

`proxy/proxy/priority.py` (signature + ordering) and `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (peer-address plumbing). One gate call site, one precedence order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `effective_priority(header_value, server_config=None, now=None, source_ip=None)` applies `apply_trust_gate(source_ip, parse_priority(header_value), server_config)` **before** the cheap-window capping, so ordering is gated-then-capped and an untrusted `high` inside the cheap window still resolves to `low`.
2. **Defence-in-depth ordering.** The trust gate is applied to the declared header value *before* the cheap-window low-capping, so a spoofed `high` during cheap hours still routes as `low` regardless of the gate.
3. `priority_from_headers(headers, server_config=None, now=None, source_ip=None)` forwards `source_ip` to `effective_priority`; the parameter is optional and keyword-compatible so every existing caller keeps working unchanged (backward compatibility).
4. `request_priority(request, server_config=None)` fallback path derives `source_ip` from the request's **direct peer** (`request.client.host`), never from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP`; when `request.client` is absent it passes `None` and the gate treats the source as untrusted only if the gate is enabled (documented behaviour, no crash).
5. `proxy/proxy/ui.py` passes `request.client.host` into the `priority_from_headers(...)` call at the request entry point (the existing `priority_decision` log line gains the resolved source and remains one line per request).
6. Downgrade is silent at the HTTP layer: no new status code, no `Retry-After`, no header rejection; `X-Priority-Applied` reports the effective (post-gate, post-cap) priority.
7. Integration tests in `proxy/tests/test_priority_trust.py` drive `priority_from_headers` (and a starred `TestClient` request through the entry point where practical) to prove: untrusted `high` → `medium` outside the cheap window; untrusted `high` → `low` inside it; trusted `high` unaffected; gate disabled → unchanged behaviour; no `source_ip` → unchanged behaviour.
8. Existing `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` suite passes unchanged (or with only signature-compatible test updates).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — gate ordering, `source_ip` parameters, peer-address fallback
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — pass `request.client.host` at the entry point
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_trust.py` — integration cases
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — regression check
